what: explicit integer MT19937 seeds for the sequence-stratified random-subset control of R1
derivation: CPython random_seed(): a non-int seed is hashed with PyObject_Hash and the result cast to size_t, so the MT19937 init key is hash((20261006, d)) mod 2**64. This is two's-complement reinterpretation of a negative hash, NOT abs(hash).
int_seed_rule: CPython random_seed() applies int.__abs__ to an int seed; every key here is already non-negative, so Random(key) seeds MT19937 with exactly these bits.
why_an_integer_is_needed: CPython 3.11 restricted seeds to None/int/float/str/bytes/bytearray, so the executed tuple expression raises TypeError there. The integer form runs everywhere.
hash_portability: hash() of a tuple of ints is not salted by PYTHONHASHSEED and is unchanged from 3.8 through 3.12, so these keys are re-derivable; str/bytes hashing IS salted, which is why a string seed would not have been safe.
note: Seeds depend only on (SEED, draw index), so all ten systems share this one mapping. No metric value and no drawn subset is changed by recording it.
